general.description: Highly specialised columnar biological organisms that grow in thin-atmosphere environments. They form tall vertical structures composed of layered, leaf-like modules that create internal chimneys for controlled atmospheric circulation. Some species exhibit external ring structures that indicate age progression.
environmental_context: Common in flat plains and low-relief terrain
Often appear as tall vertical biological towers
Internally generate regulated atmospheric flow systems
Some species exhibit visible growth rings indicating age

color_variants.rule: Color is determined by parent star type (genus-wide deterministic mapping)

Tubus sororibus.description: Clustered hollow stalk structures forming grouped vertical colonies with capped reproductive growth.

Tubus rosarium.description: Compact tubular spires with explosive reproductive pods distributed along upper segments.

Tubus cavas.description: Vertical stalk system composed of pale segmented tubes with internal gas exchange cavities.

Tubus compagibus.description: Highly segmented tubular structure with dense interlocking fronds between growth modules.

Tubus conifer.description: Tall hollow cylindrical structures capped with inverted crowns for wide-area seed dispersal.

notes.gravity_constraints: Strict maximum gravity of 0.15g applies to all species
special_rules: All species require thin atmosphere conditions
Extremely low gravity requirement makes Tubus one of the most restrictive genera
Temperature band is strictly 160K–190K for all species
Minimum sample distance is 800m due to tall, sparse distribution patterns
Structures behave like biological towers with internal atmospheric regulation
Some species show visible age rings indicating long-term growth cycles
Distribution is heavily biased toward flat plains and low-relief terrain
Tubus species function as self-regulating vertical gas exchange systems
